report_name: Ransomware Attack Cripples Japanese Cloud Provider IDCF Cloud

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Attackers
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actors responsible for the ransomware attack against IDC Frontier's IDCF Cloud service. The speed and scale of the attack suggest a sophisticated group.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The primary technique used in the ransomware attack to encrypt 3.6 PB of data across 225 databases, denying access to systems for 495 clients.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Attackers targeted 239 hypervisors to make recovery difficult and time-consuming. Deleting volume shadow copies is a common method for this technique.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: The vssadmin command-line tool was likely used by the attackers to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery, a common ransomware TTP mentioned in the report's hunting hints.

identities.name: IDC Frontier
identities.description: A major Japanese cloud and digital infrastructure provider and SoftBank subsidiary whose IDCF Cloud service was targeted by a ransomware attack.

identities.name: SoftBank Group
identities.description: The parent company of the primary victim, IDC Frontier.

identities.name: IDCF Cloud Customers
identities.description: A group of 495 corporate and local government clients affected by the service outage in the 'East Japan Region 1' data center.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b9a1c8d-e3f4-4a5b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ransomware-attack-disrupts-japans-idcf-cloud-used-by-govt-clients/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1490
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware technique to inhibit system recovery, as suggested in the article's hunting hints.
